title: Using AI-generated fictional cover art as inspectable objects in Video Store Chaos
author: InternetMammoth8482
selftext:
I'm developing Video Store Chaos solo in Unity 6 with C#. It uses generative AI for fictional movie, game and VHS cover artwork, plus some posters and video content. This is disclosed on the Steam page.

The cover art is part of an interactive sorting system. Players pick up a case, inspect both sides, read its fictional back-cover description and work out which genre shelf it belongs on. The store contains 2,592 cases across 720 fictional titles. So the challenge goes beyond producing individual nice-looking images: the front, back and genre clue have to make sense together as a game object.

For this kind of use, clear clues matter as much as visual variety. A visually convincing horror cover on something that belongs in a different genre would undermine the sorting task. The gameplay context is what makes consistency between the artwork and the case's description important.

Here's a one-minute gameplay overview showing how the covers are used in the store: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SrlNGNHxX5U

I'm happy to discuss the project and the use of generated cover textures in a Unity game. It is planned for October 2026 on Windows PC, with English and German support.
